items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: the cello player knew there was an opening, Brownie his name was, Maurice Brown, and he says, “Go over and see Roy Shields, he’s looking for a guitar player.”

ctx.x: Well how did the — you got on the NBC staff?
Yeah, well I was on about three different times on NBC. I mean when I left Vaughn Monroe I went right on NBC with the Kate Smith Show. And that was live, five days a © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
week. That’s how I got the job, the cello player knew there was an opening, Brownie his name was, Maurice Brown, and he says, “Go over and see Roy Shields, he’s looking for a guitar player.”

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: one of the cello players, Maurice Brown, told me, “hey they need a guitar player over at NBC, want to go up? He says “I’ll recommend you. So he did. And I got the job.

ctx.x: I bet Vaughn Monroe loved that. That’s a good story. When did you decide to move into New York?

Well I didn’t move into New York, I just started doing gigs. When I left Vaughn’s band luckily I had made connections, unknowingly, with all the violin players that I worked with on the Camel show. And most of them were contractors. And the rock & roll thing was hitting in New York and they were hiring a lot of guitar players. And one of the cello players, Maurice Brown, told me, “hey they need a guitar player over at NBC, want to go up? He says “I’ll recommend you. So he did. And I got the job. I started the job…
These would be for live TV shows?
